environment.level: TopoShape, as in upstream's own toponaming tests; a modelling operation is re-run with changed operands under the same tags

ground_truth.definition: outward normal + whether the face lies on the solid's bounding box (outer wall vs pocket wall)
ground_truth.rationale: Position is deliberately excluded: a parameter change is supposed to move faces, and a positional identity would report correct behaviour as corruption.
ground_truth.correction_during_the_round: The first implementation required the face plane to match exactly. It reported 4 of 10 references in S2 as silently wrong. Those were pocket walls that had legitimately moved. The defect was in the measurement, not in FreeCAD.

scenarios.name: through pocket becomes blind
scenarios.broken_detail: Face5, the -Z outer face, which lost its hole and is topologically a different face

scenarios.name: tool replaced
scenarios.broken_detail: Face7-Face10, all four pocket walls, whose generating tool no longer exists

scenarios.name: upstream feature inserted
scenarios.broken_detail: Face1, Face2, Face5: the three outer faces the inserted notch cuts into

caveats: Six scenarios on axis-aligned boxes with rectangular pockets. Not a general claim about all geometry.

The candidate counter uses the same predicate as the ground truth, so 'exactly one candidate' is partly unambiguous by construction on these shapes. It is a necessary condition for unambiguous repair, not a sufficient one. On fillets, revolved faces or many coplanar faces, ambiguity would rise and must be measured separately.
TopoShape level, not document level: the document-object path could not run because Part::Box needs the material library, which a minimal build does not install.
